scope: Primary-source audit of CHEMBL4328667 / DOI 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.8b01098 for a ROCK2 retrospective benchmark; no affinity values inferred across assays and no cloud or GPU work.

sources.title: Identification of Selective Dual ROCK1 and ROCK2 Inhibitors Using Structure-Based Drug Design
ACS Supporting Information for Hobson et al.

article_assay.construct: amino acids 11-552 (542 residues), as stated in accepted manuscript p.5; ChEMBL CHEMBL4328667 independently describes GST-fused human recombinant ROCK2 residues 11-552 expressed in Spodoptera frugiperda insect cells
article_assay.substrate_and_detection: peptide substrate; phosphorylation monitored using 33P-labeled ATP in the HTS description (article p.5)
article_assay.assay_record_details: The article p.5 describes the approximately 700,000-compound HTS with 33P-labeled ATP. The SI routine HTRF protocol (pp.S2-S3) separately specifies fluorescent streptavidin/antibody detection after the 60-minute kinase reaction; ChEMBL's compressed description combines the 33P and HTRF terms. Preserve the contexts separately rather than treating them as one unresolved readout.
article_assay.endpoint: enzyme inhibition IC50; article Table 1 reports IC50 / µM at 100 µM ATP (pp.6-7), and the SI HTRF protocol gives the routine assay conditions (pp.S2-S3)
article_assay.units_and_censoring: Table values are µM; cells such as >10 µM are right-censored bounds. ChEMBL activity records may be represented in nM and must retain original relation and units before conversion.

structure_6ED6.construct: The SI (p.S16) specifies human ROCK2 residues 27-417 with an N-terminal six-histidine/TEV purification tag for compound-12 crystallization. RCSB polymer entity 1 reports a 415-residue deposited construct sequence including the tag; this should not be described as 415 modeled protein residues or as assay residues 11-552.
structure_6ED6.structure_quality: X-ray, 2.86 Å, released PDB entry; solved pose is structural evidence only, not an affinity measurement
structure_6ED6.paper_mapping: Accepted manuscript Figure 2 caption (p.18) identifies compound 12 in ROCK2 as PDB 6ED6. Table 1 (p.7) gives compound 12 ROCK2 IC50 0.037 µM at 100 µM ATP (37 nM; no censoring).

benchmark_rows.local_curated_counts: 46 downloaded activity rows, 43 exact unique compounds, 1 right-censored retained row according to data/phase15/rock-benchmark.json; 2 excluded rows
benchmark_rows.meaning: This is a single-publication, single-assay enzyme IC50 retrospective panel with assay-derived weak observations, not a random decoy benchmark.

unresolved_or_caveats: The original article's accessible manuscript confirms the 11-552 HTS construct but does not establish that every later ROCK1/ROCK2 Table 1 measurement used exactly the same construct preparation. CHEMBL's assay description is the strongest local assay-specific record and should be cited for CHEMBL4328667 rows.

6ED6 has a 415-residue deposited construct sequence including the N-terminal tag; the SI identifies the processed ROCK2 portion as residues 27-417, while CHEMBL4328667 uses residues 11-552. These are not the same documented construct. Do not call a 6ED6-template run same-construct validation; quantify it as construct/domain transfer.

The paper's medicinal-chemistry series and PDB-linked compound are likely represented in model training data. Random splits risk analogue and publication leakage; structure-linked compounds should be excluded from training for a prospective structure-transfer test.

The article's p.5 33P statement refers to the discovery HTS, while the SI pp.S2-S3 documents the routine Table 1 HTRF assay; exact transfer of every ChEMBL row to a particular stage should still rely on CHEMBL4328667 metadata and the publication mapping.
defensibility: A larger retrospective benchmark restricted to CHEMBL4328667 is defensible for assay-specific ROCK2 IC50 prediction and split-method testing, because target, publication, assay identifier, endpoint and censoring can be kept fixed. It is not a strict same-construct benchmark when using the 6ED6 construct (ROCK2 27-417 plus tag) against the CHEMBL4328667 assay construct (11-552). The actual kinase domain is now documented, so a 415-residue structure/template condition is scientifically interpretable as a domain/construct transfer; use the documented 11-552 sequence when available, report the 6ED6 condition separately, and keep exact compounds, salts/stereoisomers and close series grouped across folds.
required_reporting: Retain target isoform, CHEMBL assay/document IDs, construct, substrate, ATP condition, readout metadata, endpoint, original unit and censoring relation for every row.
Report ROCK2 only for this panel; do not pool ROCK1, PKA, cellular pMYPT1, Kd/Ki, or CEPT/Y-27632 outcomes into this IC50 label.
Use scaffold/series or publication-held-out splits, with a structure-linked holdout policy stated before inference; random molecule splits are descriptive only.
Treat >10 µM as right-censored (or use a prespecified censored-loss/evaluation rule), never as 10 µM exact.
decision: Proceeding with the larger panel is defensible as a retrospective, assay-specific ROCK2 benchmark with explicit construct/domain transfer and leakage limits. It should not be presented as matched-construct experimental validation or prospective generalization until sequence/construct reconciliation and a held-out external assay are supplied.
